Routines for spare blankets on the job
Trainers ask staff to read this twice, and this page teaches why

Spare blankets matter because they keep pet cabins calm, clean, and ready when weather shifts or a crate needs a softer setup. At the Companion Animal Travel Desk, we treat every blanket as part of the travel check, not as an extra to handle later. New staff should keep the work area tidy, speak gently, and move with care so each animal gets steady, patient attention from Aurelia Skyways.

Use only blankets that are clean, dry, and free of loose threads, strong scents, or anything that could snag on a crate door. Fold them so they fit neatly in the storage bin and do not crowd the other supplies. If a blanket looks worn, set it aside for review instead of putting it back into circulation. That helps us keep the service consistent for travelers like Mateo Yilmaz or Amara Dubois and keeps Chester and other pets comfortable.

When a rabbit is booked, check the file before handling any bedding decision. <<FACT F064>> Keep your focus on the record and on calm handling, because the desk team needs to stay consistent from one shift to the next. If a document for a rabbit appears in the packet, review it carefully and place it with the rest of the travel papers. <<FACT F082>> Do not improvise when the form is present, and do not leave questions unresolved at the counter.

If a traveler asks for a blanket change, answer in a warm professional tone and make the swap without fuss. If the cabin is already set, replace only what is necessary and report anything unusual to the senior coordinator. Clean hands, tidy folds, and steady attention protect the animal and the gear at the same time.

What to remember is simple: keep blankets clean, keep records close, and keep your service calm.
